### Recent Papers (2025–2026)

# IMU-1: Sample-Efficient Pre-training of Small Language Models
- https://arxiv.org/pdf/2602.02522
- A validated, modern recipe for sample-efficient small-LM pretraining: combines data-centric strategies with current architectural and optimization advances into one tested pipeline. The closest thing to a 2026 cookbook for exactly our project.

# Nemotron-Flash: Towards Latency-Optimal Hybrid Small Language Models
- https://arxiv.org/pdf/2511.18890
- NVIDIA's hybrid attention/SSM small-model family designed for latency-optimal inference. Current best practice for mixing state-space blocks with attention at small scale — directly informs our hybrid layer ratio.

# Rethinking On-Policy Distillation of Large Language Models: Phenomenology, Mechanism, and Recipe
- https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.13016
- Dissects why on-policy distillation works: the teacher's per-token log-ratio acts as an implicit reward, and scaling that reward beyond standard weight can push the student PAST the teacher's boundary. Changes distillation from imitation into something closer to RL.

# A Survey of On-Policy Distillation for Large Language Models
- https://arxiv.org/pdf/2604.00626
- Maps the OPD landscape now used in production by Qwen3, DeepSeek-V4, Gemma 2 and others, including self-distillation where the model teaches itself by conditioning on privileged info (ground-truth solutions, execution feedback). Our post-training menu.

# Self-Distilled Reasoner: On-Policy Self-Distillation for Large Language Models
- https://arxiv.org/pdf/2601.18734
- Single model acts as its own teacher by conditioning on privileged information, then distilling that conditioned policy into the unconditioned one. No big teacher needed for part of the pipeline — big deal for cheap iteration.

# Probabilistic Tiny Recursive Model
- https://arxiv.org/html/2605.19943v1
- Tiny Recursive Models solve hard reasoning tasks with a tiny fraction of LLM parameters by iteratively refining a latent state; PTRM adds stochastic exploration for task-agnostic test-time compute scaling. Strongest current evidence that tiny + recursion competes with big + feedforward.

# Tiny Autoregressive Recursive Models
- https://arxiv.org/pdf/2603.08082
- Brings the recursive-refinement paradigm to autoregressive generation at tiny scale. The bridge between TRM-style puzzle solvers and an actual usable tiny LM — directly relevant to our looped-block plans.

# daVinci-LLM: Towards the Science of Pretraining
- https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.27164
- Fully-open industrial-scale study of pretraining science; core claim: pretraining sets the capability ceiling that post-training can't overcome. Justifies spending most of our effort and compute on the pretraining mix, not the finetune.

# Procedural Pretraining: Warming Up Language Models with Abstract Data
- https://arxiv.org/html/2601.21725v2
- Pretraining first on abstract procedural data (synthetic structured sequences) accelerates later training and improves natural language, code, and math. A cheap stage-0 warm-up we can generate for free before spending real tokens.

# Output Embedding Centering for Stable LLM Pretraining
- https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.02031
- Fixes output-logit divergence late in training via centering of output embeddings. Stability tricks matter disproportionately for our deep-thin, heavily-overtrained setup.

# Compress-Distill: Reasoning Trace Compression for Efficient Knowledge Distillation
- https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.05988
- Compress teacher chain-of-thought traces before distilling: students keep up to 96% of raw-trace accuracy at up to 18x better per-token efficiency. Exactly how to fit reasoning distillation into a tiny student's budget (this month's paper).

# Reasoning Compression with Mixed-Policy Distillation
- https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.08776
- Mixed-policy distillation cuts reasoning token usage up to 27% while improving benchmark scores on a 1.7B model. Shorter thinking that's also better — the right target for small reasoners.

# Towards Efficient Large Language Reasoning Models via Extreme-Ratio Chain-of-Thought Compression
- https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.08324
- 73%+ CoT token reduction with slightly improved accuracy on MATH-500 at 1.7B scale. Confirms most reasoning tokens are redundant — train the student on the distilled minimal chain.

# Revisiting the Shape Convention of Transformer Language Models
- https://arxiv.org/pdf/2602.06471
- Challenges the standard narrow-wide-narrow FFN: hourglass FFN (wide-narrow-wide) matches conventional designs up to 1B params. Fresh evidence the default block shape isn't sacred — free design space at our scale.

# Memorization Dynamics in Knowledge Distillation for Language Models
- https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.15394
- Distilled models memorize >50% less training data than standard finetuning while keeping capability. For us: distillation stores generalizable knowledge more efficiently per parameter than direct training — exactly the trade a 100M model needs.

# The Rise of Parameter Specialization for Knowledge Storage in Large Language Models
- https://arxiv.org/pdf/2505.17260
- Identifies MLP value vectors as fundamental knowledge-storage units and tracks how parameters specialize for knowledge concepts. The mechanistic handle for auditing and targeting what our tiny model stores (feeds our knowledge-accounting ideas).

# What Makes Diffusion Language Models Super Data Learners?
- https://arxiv.org/pdf/2510.04071
- Diffusion LMs extract far more learning per token than autoregressive models under multi-epoch training — analyzed mechanisms include any-order modeling and built-in data augmentation. For a data-starved tiny model doing 100 epochs, a diffusion or hybrid objective is a serious contender.

# Learn from your own latents and not from tokens: A sample-complexity theory
- https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.27734
- Theory showing latent self-prediction objectives (JEPA/data2vec style) yield huge sample-complexity gains over token-level losses. Points to auxiliary latent-prediction losses as a way to squeeze more learning from the same tokens.

# µP-scaling Small Models: Principled Warm Starts and Hyperparameter Transfer
- https://arxiv.org/html/2602.10545v1
- 2026 treatment of maximal-update parameterization specifically for small models: warm starts plus exact hyperparameter transfer from cheap proxies. Upgrades our tuning pipeline from folklore to principle.

# JustRL: Scaling a 1.5B LLM with a Simple RL Recipe
- https://arxiv.org/abs/2512.16649
- Shows a deliberately simple, stable RL recipe takes a 1.5B distilled model to strong reasoning without exotic tricks. Evidence that the post-distillation RL stage for small models can be simple and cheap — don't over-engineer it.

# Pedagogically-Inspired Data Synthesis for Language Model Knowledge Distillation
- https://arxiv.org/pdf/2602.12172
- Generates distillation data using teaching principles (scaffolding, worked examples, difficulty progression) rather than raw teacher sampling. Direct upgrade to our synthetic-curriculum data ideas.

# LoopFormer: Elastic-Depth Looped Transformers for Latent Reasoning via Shortcut Modulation
- https://arxiv.org/html/2602.11451v1
- 2026 looped-transformer design with elastic depth: shortcut modulation lets one shared block run a variable number of latent reasoning iterations efficiently. The modern version of the looped-middle-block idea we planned.

# Small Language Models (SLMs) Can Still Pack a Punch: A Survey
- https://arxiv.org/html/2501.05465v2
- Recent survey focused specifically on where SLMs match or beat larger models and which techniques got them there. Good cross-check that our chosen technique stack matches what actually worked.
